literal: Later he died in office as Administrator of Qinghe.
idiomatic: Later he died as Administrator of Qinghe.

literal: His son Zifu, because the Three Commentaries shared one canon yet differed in interpretation, therefore compiled them into one work, with both classic and commentary presented together, comparing their lengths and merits.
idiomatic: His son Zifu, finding the Three Commentaries one canon yet divergent in gloss, compiled them into a single work with text and commentary together, comparing length and merit.

literal: He happened to die before it was finished.
idiomatic: He died before the work was finished.

literal: Wei Lang, styled Youguan, was a native of Duling in Jingzhao.
idiomatic: Wei Lang, styled Youguan, came from Duling in Jingzhao.

literal: For generations his house had been a leading clan of the Three Metropolises.
idiomatic: For generations his house ranked among the leading clans of the Three Metropolises.

literal: His grandfather Kai had been Administrator of Changle and Qinghe in Jin.
idiomatic: His grandfather Kai had been Administrator of Changle and Qinghe under Jin.

literal: His father Kui had been Grand Chamberlain for Ceremonials under Murong Chui.
idiomatic: His father Kui had been Grand Chamberlain for Ceremonials under Murong Chui.

literal: Lang in youth had talent and reputation; when the Murong regime fell into disorder he took refuge at Jicheng.
idiomatic: Lang in youth had talent and standing; when the Murong house fell into disorder he took refuge at Jicheng.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Taiwu's reign he was summoned and appointed Administrator of Xianyang, then transferred to Administrator of Wudu.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Taiwu's reign he was summoned as Administrator of Xianyang, then transferred to Wudu.

literal: He died in his commandery.
idiomatic: He died in office.

literal: His son Fan, on probation as Administrator of Huashan Commandery, was granted the rank Baron of Gaoping.
idiomatic: His son Fan, acting Administrator of Huashan, was enfeoffed Baron of Gaoping.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: Fan's son Jun, styled Yingchao, was early accomplished in learning.
idiomatic: Fan's son Jun, styled Yingchao, was early accomplished in scholarship.

literal: Orphaned young, he served his grandmother and was famed for filial piety.
idiomatic: Orphaned young, he served his grandmother and was famed for filial devotion.

literal: Gentle, mild, modest, and yielding, he was praised throughout the province.
idiomatic: Gentle, mild, modest, and yielding, he was praised in his province.

literal: In the Taihe era he inherited the noble rank.
idiomatic: In the Taihe era he inherited the rank.

literal: He held the post of Commissioner of the Waters.
idiomatic: He rose to Commissioner of the Waters.

literal: When Emperor Xuanwu died, the commander Yu Zhong perverted justice and wielded punishments arbitrarily; Jun, through marriage ties with Left Vice Director Guo Zuo, was therefore killed at the same time.
idiomatic: When Xuanwu died, Commander Yu Zhong twisted justice and wielded punishments at will; Jun, allied by marriage to Left Vice Director Guo Zuo, fell with him.

literal: At the end he appealed his innocence to the Masters of Writing Yuan Qin; Qin knew the truth yet dared not set it right.
idiomatic: Facing death he appealed his innocence to Yuan Qin of the Masters of Writing; Qin knew yet dared not act.

literal: Jun sighed and said, "All my life I have done good, yet never received good's reward;
idiomatic: Jun sighed, "All my life I did good, yet never tasted good's reward;

literal: I have never done evil, yet now evil is my end. O vast Heaven above—where shall the upright turn who have no voice?"
idiomatic: I never did evil, yet evil is my end. O vast Heaven—where shall the upright cry out?"

literal: All who heard it grieved and were wounded in heart.
idiomatic: All who heard it grieved.

literal: In the first year of Xiping he was posthumously made Inspector of Luozhou with the posthumous title Upright.
idiomatic: In Xiping year 1 he was posthumously Inspector of Luozhou, posthumous title Upright.

literal: His son was Zican.
idiomatic: He left a son Zican.

literal: Zican, styled Huimao.
idiomatic: Zican was styled Huimao.

literal: When Prince of Qi Xiao Baoyin was made Inspector of Yong Province, he was brought in as chief clerk of the headquarters, then promoted Recorder.
idiomatic: When Prince of Qi Xiao Baoyin became Inspector of Yong, Zican entered as chief headquarters clerk, then Recorder.

literal: When Baoyin rebelled, Zican and his nephew Shuang held firm and would not follow, and together they fled and escaped.
idiomatic: When Baoyin rebelled, Zican and his nephew Shuang held firm, refused to follow, and fled together.

literal: When Yong Province was pacified, he was granted the rank Viscount of Chang'an.
idiomatic: When Yong was pacified he was enfeoffed Viscount of Chang'an.

literal: In the Putai era he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.
idiomatic: In Putai he rose to Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.

literal: When Emperor Xiaowu entered the passes, Zican successively held the posts of Left Director of the Mobile Office and Inspector of South Fenzhou.
idiomatic: When Xiaowu entered the passes, Zican served as Left Director of the Mobile Office and Inspector of South Fenzhou.

literal: His youngest brother Daoxie was Garrison Commander of Zhencheng.
idiomatic: His youngest brother Daoxie was Garrison Commander of Zhencheng.

literal: In the Yuanxiang era, Qi Shenwu ordered generals out on campaign; Zican and Daoxie were both captured and sent to Jinyang.
idiomatic: In Yuanxiang, Northern Qi Shenwu sent armies forth; Zican and Daoxie were captured and sent to Jinyang.

literal: Zican was repeatedly promoted to Inspector of South Yanzhou.
idiomatic: Zican rose to Inspector of South Yanzhou.

literal: At the beginning of Northern Qi Tianbao he was enfeoffed Baron of Xibo county.
idiomatic: At the opening of Qi Tianbao he was enfeoffed Baron of Xibo.

literal: Later he died as Inspector of Yuzhou with the posthumous title Loyal.
idiomatic: Later he died as Inspector of Yuzhou, posthumous title Loyal.

literal: Zican and his twelve brothers all practiced filial devotion; in mourning for their father they wasted away beyond the rites.
idiomatic: Zican and twelve brothers all practiced filial piety; mourning their father, they wasted away beyond the rites.

literal: After the burial they dwelt in huts beside the tomb and carried earth until a mound was formed.
idiomatic: After burial they lodged beside the tomb and heaped earth into a mound.

literal: His younger brother Rongliang was the most renowned.
idiomatic: Younger brother Rongliang was the most renowned.

literal: Rongliang, styled Ziyu.
idiomatic: Rongliang was styled Ziyu.

literal: Broadly learned and gifted in letters, humane in conduct and filial in devotion, he was esteemed by his age.
idiomatic: Broadly learned and literary, humane and filial, he was esteemed in his time.

literal: He held the posts of Remonstrator and Grand General of the Guard.
idiomatic: He was Remonstrator and Grand General of the Guard.

literal: At death he was posthumously made Inspector of Hezhou.
idiomatic: At death he was posthumously Inspector of Hezhou.

literal: His son Gang, styled Shiji, had moral resolve; his talent and learning won praise, and he led his native province—men called him the Impartial Judge.
idiomatic: His son Gang, styled Shiji, had moral fiber; talent and learning won praise, and he led his province—men called him the Impartial Judge.

literal: In the Kaihuang era he held the post of Chief Clerk of Zhao Prefecture.
idiomatic: Under Kaihuang he was Chief Clerk of Zhao Prefecture.

literal: He had sons Wenzong and Wenying, both well known.
idiomatic: He had sons Wenzong and Wenying, both renowned.

literal: Lang's younger cousin by the father's line, Daofu—Daofu's father Pi had been prized by Fu Jian's chancellor Wang Meng, who gave him his daughter in marriage.
idiomatic: Lang's agnatic cousin Daofu: Daofu's father Pi was prized by Wang Meng, Fu Jian's chancellor, who gave him a daughter.

literal: Serving Fu Jian, he was Administrator of Donghai.
idiomatic: Under Fu Jian he was Administrator of Donghai.

literal: When Fu Jian fell, he fled to the south and served Song as Inspector of Qinzhou.
idiomatic: When Fu Jian fell he fled south and served Song as Inspector of Qin.

literal: Daofu had will and strategy; in Song he reached the posts of Administrator of Xuyi and South Pei and Recorder of the Pacify-the-North Headquarters.
idiomatic: Daofu had will and strategy; in Song he was Administrator of Xuyi and South Pei and Recorder of the Pacify-the-North Headquarters.

literal: With Inspector of Xuzhou Xue Andu he plotted to bring the province within the fold; he was granted the rank Marquis of Gaomi and made his home in Pengcheng.
idiomatic: With Xuzhou Inspector Xue Andu he plotted to submit the province; he was enfeoffed Marquis of Gaomi and settled in Pengcheng.

literal: He died and was posthumously made Inspector of Yanzhou with the posthumous title Simple.
idiomatic: He died; posthumously Inspector of Yanzhou, posthumous title Simple.

literal: His son Xinzong, for merit in returning to the state, was separately granted the rank Marquis of Du county.
idiomatic: Son Xinzong, for merit in returning to the realm, was separately enfeoffed Marquis of Du.

literal: He held the posts of Grand Master of Palace Counsel and acting Inspector of Youzhou.
idiomatic: He was Grand Master of Palace Counsel and acting Inspector of You.

literal: He died and was posthumously made Inspector of South Yanzhou with the posthumous title Simple.
idiomatic: He died; posthumously Inspector of South Yanzhou, posthumous title Simple.

literal: Lang's cousin Chong, styled Hongji.
idiomatic: Lang's cousin Chong was styled Hongji.

literal: His father Su, styled Daoshou, had crossed the river with Liu Yizhen and held the post of Inspector of Yu Province.
idiomatic: His father Su, styled Daoshou, crossed the river with Liu Yizhen and was Inspector of Yu.

literal: Chong was ten when his father died; his mother Lady Zheng brought him into Wei, and they lodged in the Yellow and Luo region.
idiomatic: Chong was ten when his father died; Lady Zheng brought him into Wei and they settled between the Yellow and Luo.

literal: In youth he was prized and admired by his maternal uncle, Inspector of Yanzhou Zheng Yi.
idiomatic: In youth his maternal uncle, Yanzhou Inspector Zheng Yi, prized him.

literal: He held the post of Attendant in the Secretariat of the Minister of Education.
idiomatic: He was Attendant in the Secretariat of the Minister of Education.

literal: When Emperor Xiaowen took his daughter as a Worthy Lady of the Inner Palace, Chong was made Administrator of South Yingchuan.
idiomatic: When Xiaowen took his daughter as Worthy Lady, Chong was made Administrator of South Yingchuan.

literal: He did not like to pursue petty matters and would often say, "Why use small scrutiny to wound the great Way?"
idiomatic: He disliked petty prosecutions and often said, "Why wound the great Way with small scrutiny?"

literal: Officials and people were moved by him, and the commandery knew great peace.
idiomatic: Officials and people were moved; the commandery knew great peace.

literal: The emperor heard of it and commended him, granting two hundred bolts of silk.
idiomatic: The emperor heard and commended him, granting two hundred bolts of silk.

literal: When the capital was moved to Luoyang, Chong was made Impartial Judge of Sizhou.
idiomatic: At the move to Luoyang, Chong was Impartial Judge of Sizhou.

literal: Soon he was made Attendant in the Secretariat of Prince of Xianyang Yuan Xi, then again Impartial Judge of Henan Commandery.
idiomatic: Soon he was Attendant in Prince of Xianyang Yuan Xi's secretariat, then again Impartial Judge of Henan.

literal: Chong repeatedly held rating offices and was praised for uprightness.
idiomatic: Chong repeatedly held rating offices and was praised for fairness.

literal: Sent out as Administrator of Xiang Commandery, when his term ended and he should have been replaced, officials and people went to court begging that he remain; his term was extended three years.
idiomatic: Sent out as Administrator of Xiang, at term's end officials and people begged the court to keep him; his term was extended three years.

literal: Later he died.
idiomatic: Later he died.

literal: His son Youzhi, on first appointment Court Gentleman for the Imperial Audience, then Gentleman of the Secretariat and Colonel of Footsoldiers, was gradually promoted Rear and Front General and Grand Master of Palace Counsel before he died.
idiomatic: Son Youzhi entered as Court Gentleman, rose through Gentleman of the Secretariat and Colonel of Footsoldiers to Rear and Front General and Grand Master of Palace Counsel, then died.

literal: Youzhi's younger brother Xiuzhi was upright and self-contained and never spoke or acted against others.
idiomatic: Younger brother Xiuzhi was upright and reserved, never giving offense in word or deed.

literal: He held the posts of Gentleman of the Secretariat, Impartial Judge of Henan Commandery, General Who Pacifies the West, and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
idiomatic: He was Gentleman of the Secretariat, Impartial Judge of Henan, General Who Pacifies the West, and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His sons Daojian and Daoru.
idiomatic: He had sons Daojian and Daoru.

literal: Lang's cousin Zhen, styled Lingzhi—Emperor Xiaowen granted him the name.
idiomatic: Cousin Zhen, styled Lingzhi—Xiaowen granted the name.

literal: Zhen's father Shang, styled Wenshu.
idiomatic: Zhen's father Shang was styled Wenshu.

literal: He held the post of Attendant in the Secretariat of Prince of Le'an Yuan Liang.
idiomatic: He was Attendant in Prince of Le'an Yuan Liang's secretariat.

literal: He died and was posthumously made Inspector of Yongzhou.
idiomatic: He died; posthumously Inspector of Yong.

literal: Zhen in youth had moral resolve and held the post of Gentleman of the Southern Department in the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Zhen in youth had resolve and was Gentleman of the Southern Department.

literal: At the beginning of Xiaowen's reign the barbarian chief Huan Dan submitted; the court, seeking a policy to settle the frontier, made Dan Inspector of East Jingzhou and Zhen envoy to win over the barbarians of the left with him.
idiomatic: Early in Xiaowen's reign the barbarian chief Huan Dan submitted; the court made Dan Inspector of East Jing and Zhen envoy to win the left-hand tribes with him.

literal: Zhen reached Mount Tongbai, traced the Huai to its source, and proclaimed grace and favor—none failed to submit in heart.
idiomatic: Zhen reached Mount Tongbai, traced the Huai to its source, and proclaimed imperial grace—every tribe submitted in heart.

literal: At the Huai's source there had been a shrine where barbarian custom regularly used human sacrifice.
idiomatic: At the Huai's source stood a shrine where barbarian custom offered human victims.

literal: Zhen then instructed them, saying, "Heaven and earth, bright in spirit, are mankind's parents—would any parent relish the taste of a child's flesh?
idiomatic: Zhen instructed them: "Heaven and earth in their brightness are our parents—what parent savors a child's flesh?

literal: From now on you should all use wine and dried meat instead."
idiomatic: Henceforth use only wine and dried meat."

literal: The tribes obeyed the covenant, and from that time the custom was changed.
idiomatic: The tribes obeyed; the custom changed from that day.

literal: In all he won over more than seventy thousand households, established commanderies and counties, and returned.
idiomatic: He won over more than seventy thousand households, established commanderies and counties, and returned.

literal: Because his mission answered the imperial will, he was granted the rank Viscount of Bacheng.
idiomatic: For a mission that pleased the throne he was enfeoffed Viscount of Bacheng.

literal: Later, for military merit, his rank was advanced to marquis.
idiomatic: Later, for military merit, he was advanced to marquis.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to General of Manifest Martiality and Inspector of Yingzhou.
idiomatic: He rose to General of Manifest Martiality and Inspector of Ying.

literal: Wherever he served he won reputation for achievement, and the court commended him, promoting him to General of the Dragon Charger and granting two piebald horses, fifty bolts of silk, and three hundred hu of grain.
idiomatic: Wherever he served he left a record of merit; the court promoted him to General of the Dragon Charger and granted two piebald horses, fifty bolts of silk, and three hundred hu of grain.

literal: Zhen then summoned the destitute and orphaned of the province and said to them, "The Son of Heaven says I can soothe and settle you—hence these grants of grain and silk. How dare I keep them alone?"
idiomatic: Zhen summoned the province's destitute and orphaned and said, "The Son of Heaven says I can soothe you—hence grain and silk. How dare I keep them alone?"

literal: Thereupon he divided everything he had been granted among them.
idiomatic: He divided the whole grant among them.

literal: Soon he was transferred to Inspector of Jingzhou.
idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Inspector of Jing.

literal: With Masters of Writing Lu Yangwu he campaigned against Zheyang and was defeated by Qi generals Yuan Lisheng and Cai Daogong; he was dismissed and returned to his native place.
idiomatic: With Lu Yangwu of the Masters of Writing he attacked Zheyang and was beaten by Qi generals Yuan Lisheng and Cai Daogong; dismissed, he returned home.

literal: On parting he said to Yangwu, "Our lord is sage and wise and intends to swallow Wu and Yue.
idiomatic: On parting he told Yangwu, "Our lord is sage and wise and means to swallow Wu and Yue.

literal: The crux of using armies lies in the upper Yangtze.
idiomatic: The crux of war lies in the upper Yangtze.

literal: If affairs arise in Jing and Chu, I fear this old man may not be allowed to rest again."
idiomatic: If affairs stir in Jing and Chu, I fear this old man will not rest again."

literal: Later, when the imperial carriage campaigned against Deng and Mian, Zhen was again raised as Grand General of the Central Army and Chief Clerk to Prince of Pengcheng Yuan Xie.
idiomatic: Later, when the emperor campaigned against Deng and Mian, Zhen was again Grand General of the Central Army and Chief Clerk to Prince of Pengcheng Yuan Xie.

literal: When Deng and Mian were pacified, he was made acting Administrator of Luyang Commandery on probation.
idiomatic: When Deng and Mian were pacified, he was acting Administrator of Luyang on probation.

literal: When Xiaowen campaigned south again and passed through Zhen's commandery, he was made General of the Central Rampart and confirmed as Administrator.
idiomatic: When Xiaowen marched south again and passed Zhen's commandery, he was made General of the Central Rampart and confirmed Administrator.

literal: Zhen followed to Qingshui. The emperor said, "These last campaigns I have twice driven the war-chariot forth, and you have always assisted in the central army.
idiomatic: Zhen followed to Qingshui. The emperor said, "On these last campaigns I twice took the field, and you have always served the central army.
